title: Shipweek coordination timetable and notes — Apr 2026
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is the working coordination notes and timeline for the Apr 2026 Ship Week. It combines a pragmatic pre-release checklist, a compact rollout timetable (owner-by-hour), and the first draft of release notes for internal review. Treat as living — update timeline and strike items as they complete.

Quick summary:
- Release window: 2026-04-08 to 2026-04-09 (primary deploy on 2026-04-08 02:00 UTC).
- Scope: Hosted API: model catalog update (v2.7.1), serving-runtime: kernel selection optimization, console: rollout of per-route tracing toggles.
- Risk level: Medium (backend change touching request routing; fallback policy in place).

Pre-release checklist (minimum gating items) — owner in parentheses:
1) Finalized cut of release branch and validated CI green for platform and runtime (Diego).
2) Smoke test matrix created and reviewed (Lina) — include: basic generation, streaming, embeddings, cold-start latency.
3) Canary config defined and uploaded to config-store (Omar).
4) Canary capacity reservation verified with infra (Priya + infra team) — confirm GPU pool sizing for 4-hour window.
5) Rollback artifacts baked: last-known-good images tagged, DB migration no-op verified (Maya).
6) Ops playbook published to #releases with high-level runbook link (Maya).
7) Customer comms draft (status page + outbound email) ready for review (GTM) — note scheduled status page maintenance 02:00–06:00 UTC (Marketing to send).
8) Critical monitoring: alert thresholds set for 5xx spike and request latency variance; tracing flags toggled for new routes (Lina).
9) Model weights checksum & compat test for v2.7.1 (Applied ML).
10) Legal/privacy check complete for model redistribution (Legal).

Pre-deploy manual checks (within 12h):
- Confirm quota/ratelimit headers are stable on staging.
- Verify API keys for canary customers are configured to route to canary.
- Run synthetic load tests at T-6h (target 60% of expected peak).

Rollout day timetable (Owner — main contact; all times UTC):
2026-04-08 00:00 – 01:00 — Final readiness sync: core team standup (Maya).
2026-04-08 01:00 – 01:45 — Freeze: no non-release PR merges to main branches (Diego).
2026-04-08 02:00 — Begin canary deploy to 3% traffic (Omar):
  - Deploy runtime image runtime:v2026-04-08-1 to canary pool.
  - Apply canary routing policy (route 3% based on geo / customer tier).
2026-04-08 02:15 – 03:30 — Monitor canary (Lina):
  - Watch 5xx, tail logs for errors matching new routing code paths.
  - Run smoke tests against canary endpoints (embed/generate/stream).
2026-04-08 03:30 — Decision point 1: expand to 20% or rollback (Maya + SRE).
2026-04-08 04:00 — If green, expand to 20% (Omar) and continue monitoring.
2026-04-08 06:00 — Decision point 2: expand to 60% or rollback (Maya + Eng leads).
2026-04-08 07:30 — Full rollout begin (if green): ramp to 100% over next 90 minutes (Omar).
2026-04-08 09:00 — Stabilization window; begin ramp-down of extra tracing (Lina).
2026-04-08 12:00 — Post-release verification signoff; update status page (Maya).

Rollback plan (short form):
- Immediate rollback criteria: sustained 5xx > 1% for 10m, latency p95 increase > 2x baseline for 10m, or cascading service failures in dependent infra.
- Rollback action: switch routing policy to previous stable variant (runtime: stable tag), drain canary pool, and revert config-store change. Target RTO: 15–30 minutes.
- Communication: Ops lead posts to #releases and pings execs and SRE on-call.

Post-release audits & follow-ups (T+0 to T+7 days):
- T+0: Deploy tagging & release notes (Maya).
- T+1: Latency and cost delta analysis (Optimize team).
- T+3: Customer-facing changelog published (GTM).
- T+7: Retro + root-cause if any incidents (all).

Draft release notes (internal draft — for messaging review):
Title: Platform release 2026-04-08 — model catalog and runtime improvements
Highlights:
- Model catalog: added v2.7.1 of the opensource-transformer family — improves tokenization edge-cases and reduces hallucination patterns for code-gen prompts.
- Serving runtime: dynamic kernel selection enabled for attention layers — measured median token latency reduction of ~8% on 8k seq workloads (internal bench).
- Console: per-route tracing toggles exposed in the UI (Admins can opt-in tracing in-flight).
- Reliability: improved fallback routing so requests are automatically re-routed to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained.
Fixes:
- Fix for intermittent KV cache eviction under multi-tenant bursts (SERVE-2041).
- Resolved bug causing embedding indexing delay (PLAT-1907).
Known issues:
- Some legacy SDK clients (v0.9.x) may see a client-side header mismatch — recommend v1.0.2 or later.
- Minor telemetry gaps observed during the 02:00–03:00 window in one region; we are tracking (M-ops ticket created).

Communication plan (who hits which channel):
- Status page: Maintenance message at T-30m; success update at T+4h (GTM owner).
- #releases Slack: live updates from Ops (Maya).
- Customer email (enterprise): brief note at T+24h if no major regressions (GTM).
- Support play: Support docs + canned responses ready in Zendesk (Customer Success).

Open questions / blockers (to resolve before go):
- Confirm whether we should enable experimental aggressive batching on the production runtime (affects latency/cost tradeoffs) — decision required by 2026-04-06 EOD (Diego).
- Need final signoff from Legal for model redistribution text in changelog (Maya).
- Applied ML: provide final QA for v2.7.1 on long-sequence prompts (Lina to coordinate).

Appendix: quick links (working):
- Staging smoke checklist: https://confluence.redwood/c/q/staging-smoke-2026-04-01
- Primary Jira epic: PROJ-3124
- Runtime PR for kernel selection: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/889
- Platform PR for routing policy: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2713

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep decision gates tight; prefer conservative ramp if any unknown telemetry shows up.
- If rollback occurs, capture first 10 minutes of traces and attach to the incident for the retro.
- After release, create a small eval using 50 deterministic prompts to check for quality regressions (Applied ML).

---
If you are assigned an owner line above, make sure to update the doc with timestamped confirmations (e.g., "Lina — smoke tests passed 2026-04-08 02:25 UTC").
